chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Sayyari, from Muhammad ibn Jamhour, who said:

Al-Najjashy was a man from the landowners, working as an administrator over Ahvaz and Fars. So one of the people of his workforce said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'In the register of Al-Najjashy, there is taxation due upon me, and he is a believer who follows your obedience. So if you see fit, write for me a letter to him.'

He said: So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Cause gladness to your brother, Allah will cause you gladness.' He said: So when the letter reached him, he entered upon him while he was in his gathering. So when he was alone, he handed him the letter and said: 'This is the letter of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him).' So he kissed it and placed it upon his eyes, and said to him: 'What is your need?' He said: 'Taxation upon me in your register.' So he said to him: 'And how much is it?' He said: 'Ten thousand Dirhams.'

So he called his scribe and instructed him to pay it off for him. Then he released him from it and ordered that it be recorded for him for the next year. Then he said to him: 'Have I gladdened you?' So he said: 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' Then he ordered for him a mount and a maid and a slave, and ordered for him a set of clothes. During all of that, he was saying to him: 'Have I gladdened you?' So he was saying: 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' So, every time he said 'Yes', he increased for him until he was finished.
Then he said to him: 'Carry away the furnishings of this room in which you were seated when you handed over to me the letter of my Master which you brought to me, and raise your needs to me.'

He said: So he did and the man went out. So the man came to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) after that and narrated to him the story in its entirety. So he (the Imam) became joyful with what was done. So the man said: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! It is as if he has caused you to be glad, what he did with me.' So he (the Imam) said: 'Yes, by Allah! Allah and His Messenger have indeed been gladdened.'

key_terms.النَّجَاشِيُّ: Al-Najjashy, a specific administrator or landowner mentioned in the narrative
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you (a phrase of deep respect and gratitude)
key_terms.سُرَّ أَخَاكَ: Cause gladness to your brother (a key phrase in the letter)

ai.seo_question: How did the Imam facilitate the financial relief of a believer through the administrator Al-Najjashy?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s strategic use of written correspondence (kutub) to advocate for believers within administrative structures, demonstrating how spiritual authority intersects with worldly governance. The administrator’s repeated inquiry, 'Did I please you?' (hal sarartuka?), underscores the Shia ethical principle that causing joy to a fellow believer is a direct means of attaining divine pleasure, a concept deeply rooted in the Imam’s teachings on social solidarity.
